title: Fast-Slow Evolutionary Occupancy Prediction via Controlled Dynamics
claim: Fast models respond quickly but are inaccurate, and slow models are accurate but delayed; ours fuses both to get low latency and high accuracy.
layout: 3 panels: two compact baselines on top, larger method diagram below; check/cross marks
description: The figure has three panels. The top two, (a) and (b), are gray rounded boxes that show baselines as simple pipelines. Multi-view driving camera images go into a peach 'Deployment-friendly Model' in (a) or a blue 'Performance-oriented Model' in (b), and a colored 3D occupancy voxel output comes out. Under each is a pair of labels with green check marks and red crosses: latency is good and accuracy is poor in (a), and the reverse in (b). Panel (c), the larger bottom panel, is labeled 'EvoOcc (Ours)'. It shows a slow system on a top timeline and a fast system on a bottom timeline, with timestamps t0 to t5. Arrows feed both into green 'EvoOcc' blocks that output occupancy. Two shaded zones are labeled 'Joint predictions arrival' and 'Only fast predictions arrival'. Three green checks appear at the bottom: latency, high-accuracy and asynchronous.
caption: Overview of fast-slow evolutionary occupancy prediction. (a) Deployment-friendly models provide timely occupancy predictions but sacrifice geometric and semantic accuracy. (b) Performance-oriented models are more accurate, yet their delayed outputs may become stale for real-time perception. (c) EvoOcc exploits high-quality information from the slow system without sacrificing the responsiveness of the fast system by switching between two operational modes.
abstract: 3D semantic occupancy prediction provides dense geometric and semantic scene representations for autonomous driving, where both high accuracy and low response latency are crucial for safe downstream forecasting and planning. Existing methods usually exhibit different accuracy-latency characteristics. Performance-oriented models provide stronger geometric and semantic predictions, while deployment-friendly models provide faster responses. This motivates EvoOcc, a fast-slow evolutionary occupancy prediction framework that jointly exploits their complementary strengths to improve the accuracy-latency balance without changing the upstream architectures. EvoOcc models evolutionary occupancy prediction as a continuous time controlled dynamical system, enabling flexible adaptation to variable slow system delays and irregular fast system arrivals. The framework further decomposes the evolution process into dual state evolution where ego state evolution compensates for the deterministic coordinate shifts and scene state evolution models the genuine geometric and semantic scene changes. Extensive experiments on three different fast-slow system pairs and irregular prediction arrivals show that EvoOcc consistently improves over fast system baselines while maintaining much lower latency than the slow system, indicating a favorable accuracy-latency balance and stable behavior under practical inference situations.
